title: Authoritative audit escrower: KMS-backed WORM manifest and regional residency proofs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers in regulated industries require cryptographically verifiable, region-bound audit artifacts for admin operations (access grants, role changes, config drift). Current admin-audit pipeline produces event streams and snapshots, but lacks: (1) a single authoritative WORM manifest per retention epoch, (2) KMS/HSM-backed notarization of manifests, and (3) residency metadata that can be consumed by legal/evidence teams. This ticket implements an "Authoritative Audit Escrower" service that periodically bundles admin events into sealed WORM manifests, KMS-stamps the manifest digest, attaches region and retention policy metadata, and ships an escrow bundle to designated cold storage endpoints (customer vaults / escrow buckets) with tamper evidence and an indexed lookup API.
acceptance_criteria: Escrower service creates a signed WORM manifest every 24h (configurable) containing digest list and residency tag for the epoch
Manifest digest is signed using a dedicated KMS key with HSM-backed signing. Signature + certificate chain is included in bundle
Bundles uploaded to escrow storage are immutable (server-side WORM or object lock enabled) and return an immutable object URL and retention policy manifest
Lookup API returns proof objects: manifest digest, KMS signature, regional policy tag, and per-event Merkle inclusion proof for sampled events
Automated evidence export job can produce a compliance packet (manifest + signature + sample verification scripts) and a human-readable retention summary
E2E integration test that simulates cross-region admin actions and validates residency metadata is present in final bundle
Security review completed and threat mitigations documented (key rotation, key usage audit, minimal privs)
Performance: escrow bundling must not exceed 60s CPU wall-time for a 24h epoch with up to 10M admin events (streamed compose), and upload retries respect backoff policy
implementation_notes: Design service as a Kubernetes job with leader-election; leader composes manifest and rotates local temp store into immutable staging
Use AWS KMS/EKMS or customer-provided HSM via private connector for signature operations; store signature metadata in manifest.json
Compose digest list as SHA-256 per-event + epoch Merkle tree. Persist tree root and sample inclusion proofs for on-demand audit
Add residency tags at event ingestion time (region-instance, region-policy) and include on manifest level to support legal eDiscovery
Integrate with object storage lifecycle rules: set Object Lock mode compliance, retention until manifest.expiry; for S3 use PutObject with ObjectLockMode and retention headers
Provide fallback: if HSM unresponsive, escrower falls back to an ephemeral signing key stored in vault but marks bundle as 'degraded-signature' and triggers pager
Expose admin endpoints for manual re-escrow and manifest re-signing (audit-only, requires elevated role and 2-step approval)
Add metrics: manifests_created_total, manifest_sign_latency_seconds, escrow_upload_failures_total, sample_verification_pass_rate
Create migrations to re-ingest existing sealed snapshots to populate Merkle tree for backfilled epochs (opt-in), with rate limits to avoid throttling
